task_1.title: MesonToolchain aligns exe wrapper usage with runnable cross-builds
task_1.description: The Meson toolchain no longer treats every cross-build as requiring an executable wrapper. In 2.24.0, the generated `needs_exe_wrapper` behavior is aligned with Conan's runtime executability check so cross-built binaries only require a wrapper when the build environment cannot run them.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that MesonToolchain only marks cross-builds as needing an executable wrapper when Conan determines the produced binaries cannot run in the current build environment.

expectation.grounded: When `MesonToolchain` evaluates a cross-building scenario, its `needs_exe_wrapper` property should be derived from `can_run()` instead of being unconditionally enabled. If Conan reports that the built executables can run in the build context, `needs_exe_wrapper` should be disabled; if Conan reports they cannot run, `needs_exe_wrapper` should remain enabled.
expectation.conceptual: Meson-based cross-builds should only request an executable wrapper when the generated binaries are actually not runnable on the machine performing the build. Runnable cross-builds should behave like native execution for this setting.

constraints.grounded: This change must preserve wrapper usage for cross-builds where Conan cannot run the produced executables, and it must not regress Meson toolchain behavior by inferring wrapper requirements from cross-building alone. Existing non-cross-building behavior should remain unaffected.
constraints.conceptual: Do not require wrappers more broadly than necessary, and do not remove wrappers from environments that still need them. The change should narrow behavior based on real execution capability without altering unrelated toolchain behavior.

behavior: In cross-building configurations, `MesonToolchain` now bases `needs_exe_wrapper` on Conan's executable-run capability check rather than always setting it to enabled.
A cross-build that is still runnable in the build environment will no longer be treated as requiring an executable wrapper.
A cross-build whose binaries are not runnable in the build environment will continue to require an executable wrapper.
acceptance_criteria: When a project uses `MesonToolchain` in a cross-building configuration and Conan determines the target executables can run during the build, the generated Meson toolchain should indicate that no executable wrapper is needed.

When a project uses `MesonToolchain` in a cross-building configuration and Conan determines the target executables cannot run during the build, the generated Meson toolchain should indicate that an executable wrapper is needed.
When a project is not in a cross-building scenario, upgrading to 2.24.0 should not introduce a new executable-wrapper requirement.

task_3.title: Non-selectable diff markers in HTML report output
task_3.description: Upgrading to 2.24.0 changes the HTML output of `conan report diff` so diff markers remain visible in the rendered report but are no longer included when users select or copy code from added or removed lines.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that HTML reports generated by `conan report diff` let users select and copy diff content without including decorative diff symbols in the copied text, while keeping the rendered diff visually clear and aligned.

expectation.grounded: For `conan report diff` with `-f=html`, added and removed lines should still visibly show `+` and `-` markers in the rendered diff, but those markers must not be part of the selectable line content. Selecting or copying an added or removed line should yield only the line text itself. Non-modified diff lines should preserve the same visual symbol column alignment in the HTML view without introducing selectable marker characters.
expectation.conceptual: The HTML diff view should behave like a code review interface where change markers are visual aids only. Users should be able to copy code from the report cleanly, without extra diff prefixes appearing in pasted content, and the diff should remain visually aligned and easy to read.

constraints.grounded: This change applies to the HTML-formatted output of `conan report diff` and must not remove visible diff markers, alter which lines are classified as added or removed, or disturb the existing line-number and line-style presentation of the diff.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the change to copy/select behavior in the HTML report. The visible diff presentation and meaning of additions, deletions, and unchanged lines should stay the same.

behavior: In HTML diff output, added lines display a visible `+` marker that is separate from the selectable line text.
In HTML diff output, removed lines display a visible `-` marker that is separate from the selectable line text.
When users select or copy added or removed lines from the rendered HTML report, the copied text excludes the diff marker and contains only the line content.
Non-added and non-removed lines retain alignment with the diff symbol column in the HTML view without adding selectable marker text.
acceptance_criteria: Given an HTML diff report with added lines, when a user selects and copies an added line from the rendered page, the pasted text should not include a leading `+`, while the report should still visibly show that line as added.

Given an HTML diff report with removed lines, when a user selects and copies a removed line from the rendered page, the pasted text should not include a leading `-`, while the report should still visibly show that line as removed.

When viewing a mixed HTML diff, unchanged lines should remain visually aligned with added and removed lines, and the existing diff readability cues such as line styling and numbering should remain intact.

task_2.title: Workspace super-install honors layout() source folders
task_2.description: Upgrading to 2.24.0 changes Conan workspace super-install so editable packages are resolved through each recipe's layout() source folder instead of assuming sources live at the project root. This allows workspaces with custom source layouts to super-install correctly and makes the reported package build order show the resolved folder for each editable package.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `workspace super-install` follows each editable recipe's `layout()` when locating workspace package sources, so workspaces continue to install correctly even when a project stores its build inputs under a custom source subfolder.

expectation.grounded: When `workspace super-install` processes editable packages, it should evaluate each recipe's `layout()` and resolve the package folder from the workspace project base plus `conanfile.folders.source`. The resolved folder used for the workspace build order should be normalized, and the build-order output should identify each package reference together with that resolved folder.
expectation.conceptual: `workspace super-install` should use the same source location rules that the recipe declares through `layout()`. Users should be able to super-install a workspace successfully whether a package keeps its sources at the project root or inside a declared source subdirectory, and the reported build order should clearly show which folder each package is coming from.

constraints.grounded: This behavior applies to editable packages participating in workspace super-install. The change must preserve normal workspace ordering semantics while switching folder resolution from the project root to the `layout()`-derived source folder, and any failure raised while evaluating `layout()` should surface as a regular layout-related recipe error.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only change how workspace editable package source locations are resolved and reported. It must not introduce a different workflow for users beyond honoring declared layouts and surfacing layout-related failures normally.

behavior: `workspace super-install` now evaluates `layout()` for editable workspace packages before calculating their source folder.

The folder associated with each editable package in workspace build ordering is derived from the workspace package location plus the recipe's declared source folder, instead of assuming the package root itself is the source folder.
Resolved workspace package folders are normalized before they are passed through the super-install flow.
The package build-order output now reports both the package reference and its resolved folder, making the selected workspace source location visible to users.
acceptance_criteria: When an editable workspace package declares a custom source folder through `layout()`, running `workspace super-install` should use that source folder for the workspace package instead of the workspace project root.
When an editable workspace package uses the default source location, running `workspace super-install` should still succeed without requiring any special user action.
When `layout()` raises an error during workspace super-install, the command should fail with the corresponding layout-related recipe error rather than silently ignoring the layout.
When workspace build order is reported during super-install, each editable package entry should include the resolved folder being used for that package.

task_5.title: Show missing packages in HTML dependency graphs
task_5.description: The upgrade adds user-visible handling for missing dependency resolution in HTML graph output. When graph generation encounters a missing package, the resulting graph should still represent that missing requirement visually and the reported error should identify which package or CLI request required it.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that missing dependencies are represented in `graph.html` output and that missing-package errors indicate which graph node requested the unresolved package.

expectation.grounded: When `graph info --format=html` encounters a `GraphMissingError`, the exported HTML graph should recognize the serialized error type `missing` and render the unresolved requirement as a visible graph node connected from the requiring node. The missing error payload should expose the requesting node identity, the unresolved requirement reference, and the underlying resolution failure so the formatter can show the missing relationship. The user-facing missing-package error string should also include the package or CLI origin that required the unresolved reference.
expectation.conceptual: If dependency graph generation fails because a package cannot be resolved, the HTML graph should still show where the failure happened instead of silently omitting it. Users should be able to see both the missing package and which dependency path requested it, and textual error reporting should name the requester.

constraints.grounded: Missing-package handling should be additive to existing graph error rendering and should not change the existing conflict or provide-conflict behaviors. The HTML formatter should only render a missing marker when the graph error type is `missing`, and it should preserve normal node filtering rules for unrelated build or test nodes. Existing graph generation should continue to return graph data structures even when a missing dependency is present.
constraints.conceptual: The new behavior should extend error visualization for missing dependencies without regressing other graph error displays or normal graph rendering. It should only appear for actual missing-dependency failures and should keep the rest of the graph behavior consistent.

behavior: HTML graph output recognizes missing-dependency graph errors as a distinct error category.
When a dependency is missing, the graph includes a dedicated visible node for the unresolved package reference.
The graph connects the requiring package node to the missing package node so the broken dependency path is explicit.
The missing relationship is presented as an error-style edge in the HTML visualization rather than being omitted from the graph.
Serialized missing graph errors now carry the requiring node identity, the unresolved requirement, and the underlying resolution error details.
Stringified missing-package errors include the package reference that required the unresolved dependency, or indicate that the request originated from the CLI when no package node is available.
acceptance_criteria: When `graph info --format=html` is run for a graph with an unresolved dependency, it should still produce HTML output that visually shows the missing package as part of the graph.
When a package depends on a missing requirement, the HTML graph should show a connection from that package to the missing requirement so the source of the failure is visible.
When the unresolved dependency originates from a top-level CLI request rather than another package node, the missing-package error text should identify the CLI as the requester.
When graph generation fails for reasons other than a missing dependency, existing error-specific graph behavior should remain unchanged.
When no dependency is missing, graph rendering and error reporting should behave as before without introducing missing-package markers.

task_4.title: Public Conan Python sub-APIs expanded
task_4.description: Conan 2.24.0 formalizes additional Python sub-APIs as supported entry points on ConanAPI and clarifies their typed contracts for cache access, lockfile resolution, diff reporting, vulnerability auditing, and backup-source upload workflows.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Python integrations can rely on the additional Conan 2.24.0 sub-APIs as supported public interfaces, with clear contracts for cache archive restore/save, lockfile retrieval, recipe and source diff generation, audit access, and backup-source upload behavior.

expectation.grounded: `ConanAPI` should expose `cache`, `lockfile`, `audit`, and `report` as public sub-APIs. The supported contracts should include `CacheAPI.save(package_list: PackagesList, tgz_path, no_source=False) -> None`, `CacheAPI.restore(path) -> PackagesList`, `LockfileAPI.get_lockfile(lockfile=None, conanfile_path=None, cwd=None, partial=False, overrides=None) -> Lockfile`, and `UploadAPI.upload_backup_sources(files: List) -> None`. `ReportAPI.diff(old_reference, new_reference, remotes, old_path=None, new_path=None, cwd=None)` should remain the public way to compare recipe and source differences between two references or exported local paths.
expectation.conceptual: The library should provide officially supported Python entry points for cache operations, lockfile handling, vulnerability auditing, and version-to-version diff reporting, with stable return contracts that callers can depend on when automating Conan workflows.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable lockfile lookup rules described by `LockfileAPI.get_lockfile`: an explicit path must exist, an explicit empty string disables implicit `conan.lock` discovery, and an omitted lockfile still performs default lookup relative to the conanfile location or current working directory without failing when no default lockfile is present. Preserve `CacheAPI.restore` failure on a missing archive via `ConanException`, `CacheAPI.get_backup_sources` filtering by `package_list`, `exclude`, and `only_upload`, and `ReportAPI.diff` behavior of resolving references from cache or remotes when local paths are not supplied.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should expand supported Python API coverage without regressing existing cache, lockfile, diff, or backup-source workflows. Default discovery and error behavior should stay consistent, and callers should not need to infer undocumented side effects.

behavior: `ConanAPI.cache`, `ConanAPI.lockfile`, `ConanAPI.audit`, and `ConanAPI.report` are treated as supported Python-facing sub-APIs.
`CacheAPI.restore(path)` returns a `PackagesList` describing restored recipes and packages and raises `ConanException` when the specified archive file does not exist.
`CacheAPI.save(...)` accepts a `PackagesList` input for cache export selection and completes as a side-effecting operation without a return payload.

`LockfileAPI.get_lockfile(...)` returns a `Lockfile` and preserves the distinction between an omitted lockfile, an explicit lockfile path, and an explicit empty string that disables automatic default lockfile discovery.

`ReportAPI.diff(...)` compares recipe and source differences between two references, sourcing data from cache or remotes when no local path is provided and supporting exported local paths when they are supplied.
`UploadAPI.upload_backup_sources(files)` uploads previously gathered backup-source files as a side-effecting operation without returning a value.
acceptance_criteria: When a Python consumer accesses `ConanAPI.cache`, `ConanAPI.lockfile`, `ConanAPI.audit`, or `ConanAPI.report`, those interfaces should be usable as supported sub-APIs for automation code.
When `CacheAPI.restore()` is called with an existing archive, it should return a `PackagesList`; when called with a nonexistent archive, it should fail with `ConanException`.

When `LockfileAPI.get_lockfile()` is called with `lockfile=""`, it should not auto-load a default `conan.lock`; when `lockfile` is omitted, it should attempt default lookup relative to the conanfile path or current working directory without treating the absence of that default file as an error.

When `ReportAPI.diff()` is called without local paths, it should resolve the compared recipes from cache or remotes; when local paths are provided, it should compare the exported local content for those references.
When backup source files are collected for upload, `UploadAPI.upload_backup_sources()` should perform the upload as an action-oriented API without returning a result object.

task_6.title: Add structured JSON results for cache integrity checks
task_6.description: The cache integrity command now supports a machine-readable JSON result that identifies corrupted cache artifacts, while preserving integrity validation and failure signaling for corrupted recipes or packages.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache check-integrity` can expose corrupted cache artifacts in a structured JSON format so users and tooling can identify and act on damaged recipes or packages without losing the command's existing corruption detection behavior.

expectation.grounded: `conan cache check-integrity` should support JSON-formatted output that serializes corrupted artifacts under a `Local Cache` result section. `CacheAPI.check_integrity(package_list, return_pkg_list=True)` should return a `PackagesList` containing corrupted entries instead of immediately raising, while `CacheAPI.check_integrity(package_list, return_pkg_list=False)` should continue to raise `ConanException` when corruption is detected. If a recipe is corrupted, the returned result should contain the recipe reference and treat its packages as corrupted without enumerating package references from additional binary checks; if the recipe is valid but some binaries are corrupted, the result should include the owning recipe and the corrupted package references.
expectation.conceptual: The integrity-check command should provide a machine-readable summary of corrupted cache contents, not just human-readable console logs. Consumers should be able to retrieve the set of corrupted artifacts programmatically, and corruption should still be treated as a failed integrity check. Recipe-level corruption should be reported at the recipe scope, while binary-only corruption should identify the affected packages.

constraints.grounded: Integrity verification must remain limited to the selected references and packages. The structured result must list only corrupted artifacts, and a clean run must produce an empty corrupted-artifact result and no failure. Existing exception-based behavior must remain unchanged for callers that do not opt into `return_pkg_list=True`.
constraints.conceptual: The new output must add structured reporting without weakening existing validation semantics. Clean artifacts should not be misreported, corrupted artifacts should still cause the operation to fail, and existing consumers that rely on exception-based failure should continue to behave as before unless they explicitly request structured results.

behavior: The cache integrity command can emit a JSON payload that represents corrupted artifacts in a structured result keyed by `Local Cache`.
The integrity-check API can return a `PackagesList` of corrupted artifacts when structured consumption is requested, instead of always failing immediately.
If a recipe is corrupted, the result marks the recipe as corrupted and does not continue with per-package corruption checks for that recipe.
If a recipe is valid but one or more packages are corrupted, the result includes the recipe and the specific corrupted package references.
Corruption continues to be a failure condition for the command even when structured JSON results are produced.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan cache check-integrity` with JSON output enabled and corrupted cache entries exist, it should return a structured result containing the corrupted artifacts under a `Local Cache` section.
When the selected recipe metadata is corrupted, the reported result should identify the recipe as corrupted and should not require individual package entries for that recipe.
When the recipe is intact but specific binaries are corrupted, the reported result should identify the owning recipe and the affected package references.
When no corrupted artifacts are found, the command should complete without a corruption failure and the structured corrupted-artifact result should be empty.
When library consumers call `CacheAPI.check_integrity` without requesting structured results, corruption should still be surfaced as a `ConanException`.

task_8.title: Allow hashlib in global.conf templates
task_8.description: The upgrade expands the Jinja2 rendering context for global.conf so users can compute hashes while deriving configuration values, enabling stable hashed paths and similar dynamic settings without external preprocessing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `global.conf` templates can derive configuration values from hashes by using `hashlib` during Jinja2 rendering, so users can generate deterministic values such as shortened or hashed paths directly in configuration.

expectation.grounded: During `global.conf` Jinja2 rendering, the template context must expose the Python `hashlib` module alongside the existing injected context values. Templates must be able to call `hashlib` APIs to compute derived strings from available inputs such as `conan_home_folder`, and the rendered result must then be loaded as normal configuration content.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to write dynamic `global.conf` templates that compute hash-based configuration values directly at render time, and those computed values should behave like any other rendered configuration setting.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to the Jinja2 render context for `global.conf`. Existing injected template variables and standard configuration loading behavior must remain available, and configurations that do not use `hashlib` must continue to render and load the same way as before.
constraints.conceptual: The new hashing capability should extend template expressiveness without changing the behavior of existing configurations or requiring users to rewrite non-hash-based settings.

behavior: `global.conf` Jinja2 templates can reference `hashlib` during rendering.
Hash-based expressions can be used to derive configuration values before the rendered configuration is parsed.
Computed hash output can be incorporated into user-facing settings such as generated storage paths or other deterministic identifiers.
Configurations that do not use the new hashing capability continue to follow the existing rendering and loading flow.
acceptance_criteria: When a `global.conf` template uses `hashlib` to derive a value, the configuration should render successfully and load the computed value as the effective setting.
When a user derives a configuration value from an existing template variable using `hashlib`, the resulting setting should reflect the deterministic hash output produced at render time.
When `global.conf` contains no `hashlib` usage, rendering and configuration loading should remain unchanged from prior behavior.
When users need shortened or hash-based derived values in `global.conf`, they should be able to express them directly in the template without external preprocessing.

task_7.title: Add workspace completion for intermediate packages
task_7.description: Conan 2.24.0 adds a `conan workspace complete` command that can automatically open or add intermediate packages needed to make a partially opened workspace valid. The upgrade also makes workspace graph validation fail explicitly when cached packages still depend on editable workspace packages, so users are guided toward completing the workspace instead of manually debugging mixed cache/editable dependency chains.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan workspaces can be completed automatically when editable packages are separated by intermediate cached packages, so users can turn those intermediate dependencies into workspace entries without manual discovery and receive actionable guidance when an incomplete workspace definition is invalid.

expectation.grounded: Expose a new `conan workspace complete` command that uses the selected profiles, lockfile, remotes, and update settings to compute dependency graphs for packages already present in the workspace. The command must detect non-editable intermediate packages whose transitive dependencies include editable workspace packages, then add them to the workspace; if a local recipe checkout for an intermediate package is not present yet, the command must open that package into the workspace before adding it. If the workspace is empty or no such intermediate packages are found, the command should succeed as a no-op. Workspace graph validation during workspace operations must reject cached packages that depend on editable workspace packages and point users to `conan workspace complete` as the remediation path.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run one command to complete a partially opened workspace when intermediate dependencies sit between workspace packages. The command should reuse existing local package checkouts when available, fetch or open missing intermediate packages when needed, and otherwise leave the workspace unchanged if there is nothing to add. If users try to operate on an incomplete workspace that still mixes cached packages above editable workspace packages, Conan should fail clearly and direct them to the workspace completion flow.

constraints.grounded: Only intermediate packages that are currently non-editable and that transitively depend on editable workspace packages should be added. Editable packages already in the workspace and ordinary cached dependencies with no transitive dependency on workspace packages must not be added by completion. Empty workspaces and graphs with no qualifying intermediate packages must remain successful no-op cases. Attempts to add a workspace entry with a missing recipe file must raise a regular Conan error instead of relying on an assertion failure.
constraints.conceptual: Workspace completion should be narrowly scoped to the missing packages required to make the workspace graph coherent. It should not pull unrelated dependencies into the workspace, it should not treat no-op situations as errors, and it should surface missing recipe problems as explicit user-facing failures.

behavior: A new `conan workspace complete` CLI subcommand is available for completing partially opened workspaces.
Running `conan workspace complete` on an empty workspace succeeds without changes and reports that there is nothing to complete.
The completion command analyzes the dependency graph of each workspace package and finds cached intermediate packages whose transitive dependencies include editable workspace packages.
Each identified intermediate package is added to the workspace as an editable package.
If an identified intermediate package does not already have a local recipe checkout in the workspace, the command opens the package into the workspace first and then adds it.

Workspace operations that build or process dependency graphs now fail with a workspace-definition error when a cached package depends on workspace packages, and that error points users to `conan workspace complete`.
Adding a workspace package with a missing recipe file now fails with an explicit Conan exception instead of an assertion-based crash.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan workspace complete` on an empty workspace, it should complete successfully, make no workspace changes, and report that there is nothing to complete.

When a workspace contains packages whose dependency graph includes cached intermediate packages that transitively depend on editable workspace packages, running `conan workspace complete` should add those intermediate packages to the workspace.
When an intermediate package already has a local checkout suitable for workspace use, workspace completion should add that package directly without requiring the user to open it manually first.
When an intermediate package needed for completion does not yet have a local workspace checkout, workspace completion should open the package into the workspace and then add it automatically.

When a user runs a workspace operation against an incomplete workspace where cached packages still depend on editable workspace packages, the operation should fail with a clear workspace-definition error that directs the user to `conan workspace complete`.
When a workspace entry is added from a missing recipe location, Conan should raise a regular user-facing error rather than terminating through an assertion failure.

task_10.title: Generate CMakeConfigDeps targets for framework-only and define-only dependencies
task_10.description: The CMake dependency generator now produces imported targets for Conan packages and components that contribute only preprocessor definitions or platform frameworks. This fixes consumption of dependencies such as macOS OpenGL-style packages that previously exported no normal libraries or include paths and therefore failed to generate a usable CMake target.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps generates consumable targets for dependencies that expose only compiler definitions and/or frameworks, so downstream CMake projects can depend on them without missing-target failures.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps processes a non-executable package or component, it should emit an imported target whenever its cpp_info exposes package frameworks, frameworks, include directories, libraries, system libraries, or preprocessor definitions. Packages or components that only define cpp_info.frameworks or only define cpp_info.defines must still generate a target, and exported definitions must be propagated as distinct CMake definition entries rather than a single space-joined value.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading should let CMake consumers use Conan dependencies that contribute only metadata such as frameworks or compile definitions. Those dependencies should behave like normal generated targets, and any exported definitions should reach downstream builds in a form CMake can apply correctly.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing rule that executable-only entries do not generate a library target. Do not regress target generation or dependency propagation for packages that already expose regular libraries, include directories, system libraries, or package frameworks.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should expand support for metadata-only dependencies without changing the behavior of ordinary library dependencies or treating executables as linkable library targets.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps now generates an imported target for a package or component whose exported metadata consists only of cpp_info.frameworks.
CMakeConfigDeps now generates an imported target for a package or component whose exported metadata consists only of cpp_info.defines.
Downstream dependencies on these framework-only or define-only packages/components resolve through the generated target instead of failing because no target was created.
Exported cpp_info.defines are propagated as separate definition entries, preserving correct downstream compile-definition semantics in generated CMake metadata.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan package exports only frameworks through cpp_info.frameworks, generating CMakeConfigDeps files should still produce a consumable imported target for that dependency.
When a Conan package or component exports only compile definitions through cpp_info.defines, generating CMakeConfigDeps files should still produce a consumable imported target for that dependency.
When another package depends on one of these metadata-only dependencies, CMake dependency generation should complete without missing-target errors caused by the dependency being omitted.
When multiple compile definitions are exported, downstream CMake consumers should receive them as separate definitions rather than one merged definition string.

task_11.title: Warn on ineffective version ranges in reference patterns
task_11.description: Version 2.24.0 adds a runtime warning when a reference pattern includes version-range syntax in a matching context where ranges are ignored. This helps users avoid assuming that selectors such as package-scoped option patterns can filter by version range, while preserving the prior matching behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that reference patterns do not silently accept version-range syntax in contexts where version ranges have no effect, and clearly warn users that only the supported consumer and wildcard forms are meaningful there.

expectation.grounded: When reference-pattern matching receives a pattern containing bracketed version-range syntax, it should emit a warning tagged as risk indicating that the version range has no effect in that context. Matching should still proceed with the existing reference-pattern semantics, and this context should continue to support only '&' for the consumer reference and '*' as a wildcard.
expectation.conceptual: If a user writes a package selector with a version range in a place where range matching is not supported, the tool should clearly warn that the range will be ignored. The operation should still continue using the normal selector behavior instead of treating the range as a valid filter.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the actual match outcome for existing reference patterns; this update only adds a warning for ineffective version-range syntax. Patterns without version-range syntax must keep their current behavior, and supported special forms using '&' or '*' must remain valid.
constraints.conceptual: This change is informational, not a new matching capability. Existing selectors should keep behaving the same unless they now surface a warning that previously missing range syntax was being ignored.

behavior: Reference patterns that include bracketed version-range syntax now produce a runtime warning that the range is ineffective in this matching context.
After the warning is emitted, matching still continues under the pre-existing reference-pattern rules rather than performing version-range selection.
The matching context continues to recognize only the consumer placeholder '&' and the wildcard '*' as supported special pattern forms called out for this usage.
acceptance_criteria: When a user applies a reference-scoped selector such as an option pattern containing a bracketed version range, the command should emit a warning that the version range has no effect.
When such a selector is used, the operation should continue with the existing non-range matching behavior instead of filtering packages by version range.
When a selector uses supported wildcard or consumer-reference notation without a version range, it should continue to behave as before without introducing this new warning.

task_9.title: Declarative Configuration Package Installs
task_9.description: Conan 2.24.0 expands experimental configuration package installation so users can install one or more config packages from a `conanconfig.yml` manifest, optionally resolve them from manifest-provided URLs, and update configuration packages with explicit safeguards around order changes. The update also normalizes persisted config requirements to recipe-level references and separates config-require lockfile upgrades into a dedicated flow.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan config install-pkg` supports a declarative `conanconfig.yml` workflow for installing multiple configuration packages, preserves predictable configuration ordering across repeated installs and updates, and prevents unsafe reordering of already-installed configuration packages unless the user explicitly forces it. Ensure that persisted configuration state and lockfile config requirements are tracked at the recipe-reference level so lockfile-driven and repeated configuration installs remain stable across binary package changes.

expectation.grounded: `conan config install-pkg` should accept either a configuration package reference or a path that resolves to `conanconfig.yml`, including the current directory by default. `conanconfig.yml` should support a `packages` list of configuration `RecipeReference`s and an optional `urls` list used as remotes for resolution. The command should fetch and install each resolved configuration package, persist installed configuration versions as `RecipeReference`s, and write lockfile `config_requires` entries as recipe references. Re-running the command with the same resolved references and order should skip re-installation unless `--force` is provided. Updates that preserve the existing installed order should be allowed, while requests that reorder already-installed configuration packages should raise `ConanException` unless `--force` is used. Config-require lockfile upgrades should be handled through `conan lock upgrade-config`, and configuration package installs should exclude Conan package metadata files from the applied configuration payload.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare configuration packages in a manifest and install them in a predictable sequence, with optional package source URLs bundled alongside that manifest. Conan should treat repeated installs as no-ops when nothing changed, allow safe version updates and additions that preserve the established order, and require an explicit force action before applying a request that would reorder existing configurations. Persisted config state and lockfiles should identify configuration requirements by recipe rather than by resolved binary package, and config lockfile upgrades should follow a dedicated CLI path.

constraints.grounded: Only packages that resolve as configuration recipes and have no dependencies should remain valid install targets for this workflow. Installing or updating config packages must not silently change the relative order of already-installed configuration recipes unless `--force` is set. If no package reference is given, `conan config install-pkg` should only proceed when a resolvable `conanconfig.yml` exists. Lockfile upgrade flows should error when no specified or default lockfile is available. Standard Conan package metadata files such as `conaninfo.txt` and `conanmanifest.txt` must not be installed as configuration content.
constraints.conceptual: Do not accept non-configuration packages or configuration packages with dependencies as valid config installs. Do not silently reshuffle previously applied configuration layers. Do not let binary package identity differences create duplicate configuration entries for the same recipe. Do not apply package bookkeeping files as if they were user configuration.

behavior: `conan config install-pkg` can now install configuration from either a single package reference or a `conanconfig.yml` manifest, with directory inputs resolving to that manifest file.
A `conanconfig.yml` manifest can declare multiple configuration packages in `packages` and optional package source URLs in `urls`.
Configuration installs resolve all requested packages first, then apply them in manifest or request order and persist the resulting installed configuration set by recipe reference.
Repeated installs of the same resolved configuration recipes in the same order are treated as a no-op unless `--force` is provided.
Configuration updates that append new packages or refresh versions without disrupting the previously established order are allowed and persisted.
Configuration updates that would change the order of already-installed configuration recipes fail unless `--force` is explicitly supplied, in which case the new order is accepted.

Lockfile `config_requires` are stored and updated as recipe references, and config-require upgrades use a dedicated `conan lock upgrade-config` flow instead of the general `conan lock upgrade` command.
Installing configuration from packages excludes Conan metadata files from the resulting applied configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid `conanconfig.yml` containing multiple configuration package references, when `conan config install-pkg` is run against that manifest or its containing directory, then Conan should resolve and install all listed configuration packages in the declared order.
Given a `conanconfig.yml` that also declares `urls`, when required configuration packages are not otherwise resolvable from configured remotes, then Conan should use those URLs during resolution.

When the requested configuration packages resolve to the same recipe references in the same order as the currently installed configuration and `--force` is not supplied, the command should skip re-installation and leave the installed configuration state unchanged.

When the requested configuration packages introduce new configuration recipes or updated recipe versions without changing the relative order of already-installed configurations, the command should complete successfully and persist the updated recipe-level configuration set.

When the requested configuration install would reorder previously installed configuration recipes and `--force` is not supplied, the command should fail and preserve the existing installed configuration state.
When `--force` is supplied for an identical install or an order-changing install, the command should proceed and persist the requested configuration state and order.

When configuration requirements are written to or upgraded in a lockfile, the resulting lockfile should track config requirements by recipe reference, and config-require upgrades should be performed through the dedicated config lock upgrade command.

task_12.title: Clarify MSBuildToolchain compile_options contract
task_12.description: The update clarifies the user-facing meaning of MSBuildToolchain compile_options so it is documented as compiler option entries for the generated ClCompile section, not as preprocessor definitions. It also makes clear that configuration supplied through the MSBuild toolchain compile_options conf is merged into that mapping.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `MSBuildToolchain` documentation correctly describes `compile_options` as compiler options applied to MSBuild `ClCompile` settings, and clearly communicates how configuration-provided compile options participate in the generated toolchain behavior.

expectation.grounded: `MSBuildToolchain.compile_options` should be documented as a dictionary of compile options that are emitted as option entries in the `ClCompile` section. The documented behavior should align with `tools.microsoft.msbuildtoolchain:compile_options` being read as a dictionary and merged into `MSBuildToolchain.compile_options` before generation.
expectation.conceptual: Users should understand that `compile_options` controls MSBuild compiler options, not preprocessor definitions, and that options supplied through the MSBuild toolchain configuration are combined with the toolchain's compile option mapping.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public meaning of `preprocessor_definitions` or `compile_options`. Preserve the existing expectation that `tools.microsoft.msbuildtoolchain:compile_options` is a dictionary input and that its values augment the generated compile-option state rather than redefining unrelated settings.
constraints.conceptual: The update should remove ambiguity without altering existing toolchain behavior. It should clarify the boundary between compiler options and preprocessor definitions and keep configuration-based compile options additive.

behavior: `MSBuildToolchain.compile_options` is treated as a dictionary of compiler option entries for MSBuild `ClCompile` output.
Configuration from `tools.microsoft.msbuildtoolchain:compile_options` is retrieved as a dictionary and merged into the toolchain's compile options.
`compile_options` is distinct from `preprocessor_definitions` and should not be described as defining preprocessor macros.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the `MSBuildToolchain` API description for `compile_options`, it should describe compiler option entries written to MSBuild `ClCompile` settings.
When a user provides `tools.microsoft.msbuildtoolchain:compile_options`, the documented contract should state that those options are combined with `MSBuildToolchain.compile_options`.
When users compare `compile_options` with `preprocessor_definitions`, the documentation should clearly distinguish compiler options from preprocessor definitions.

task_13.title: Detect Visual Studio 18 during Conan profile auto-detection
task_13.description: Conan 2.24.0 updates MSVC profile auto-detection so Visual Studio 18 (2026) is recognized during `conan profile detect`. This lets Windows users with the new IDE generate the expected detected profile and ensures the newest supported Visual Studio version is chosen when multiple supported installations exist.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that automatic Conan profile detection recognizes Visual Studio 18 (2026) when detecting MSVC toolchains on Windows.

expectation.grounded: When `conan profile detect` performs MSVC IDE discovery, it should include Visual Studio 18 in the supported IDE versions it checks through the existing Visual Studio installation and environment-based detection flow. If version 18 is present, it should be selected as the detected IDE version before falling back to versions 17, 16, and 15.
expectation.conceptual: Users with Visual Studio 18 installed should be able to rely on Conan's automatic profile detection to identify that IDE correctly, and systems with multiple supported Visual Studio versions should prefer the newest supported one.

constraints.grounded: Detection behavior for Visual Studio 17, 16, and 15 must remain unchanged aside from the addition of version 18 ahead of them in the search order. Systems without Visual Studio 18 should continue using the existing fallback behavior and detection signals.
constraints.conceptual: Adding support for the new Visual Studio release must not regress profile detection for older supported Visual Studio installations or change behavior on machines where the new version is not installed.

behavior: `conan profile detect` now considers Visual Studio 18 a supported IDE version during MSVC auto-detection.
If Visual Studio 18 is discoverable through the normal installation lookup or environment-driven discovery path, it is selected as the detected IDE version.
When more than one supported Visual Studio version is installed, Visual Studio 18 is preferred over versions 17, 16, and 15.
If Visual Studio 18 is not present, detection continues to evaluate previously supported Visual Studio versions in the existing fallback order.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan profile detect` runs on a Windows machine with Visual Studio 18 installed and no newer supported Visual Studio version available, it should detect Visual Studio 18 instead of skipping it.
When `conan profile detect` runs on a machine with both Visual Studio 18 and an older supported Visual Studio version installed, it should choose Visual Studio 18 as the detected IDE version.
When `conan profile detect` runs on a machine without Visual Studio 18 but with Visual Studio 17, 16, or 15 installed, it should continue to detect the highest available previously supported version.
When Visual Studio 18 is not discoverable, the command's MSVC profile detection behavior should remain consistent with prior supported-version fallback behavior.

task_14.title: Correct sysroot flags for QNX qcc in GNU toolchains
task_14.description: The upgrade fixes how Conan's GNU-based toolchains emit sysroot flags when a project targets QNX with the qcc compiler. Instead of always using the generic GNU --sysroot form, the toolchains now emit the compiler-compatible isysroot forwarding form for qcc while preserving existing behavior for other compilers and for builds without a configured sysroot.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that configuring a sysroot through Conan's GNU toolchains works correctly for QNX builds that use the qcc compiler, so generated build flags are accepted by the compiler and existing sysroot behavior remains unchanged for other toolchains.

expectation.grounded: When `AutotoolsToolchain` or `GnuToolchain` reads `tools.build:sysroot`, it must compute `sysroot_flag` according to the active compiler. If `settings.compiler` is `qcc`, the generated sysroot flag must use the qcc-compatible `-Wc,-isysroot,<path>` form. For any other compiler, the generated flag must continue to use the `--sysroot <path>` form. The sysroot path must still be normalized to forward slashes before being emitted, and no `sysroot_flag` should be produced when `tools.build:sysroot` is unset or empty.
expectation.conceptual: When a user sets a sysroot for GNU-style Conan toolchains, the generated compiler and linker flags should match the selected compiler's expected syntax. QNX builds using `qcc` should receive a compiler-compatible sysroot option, while other compilers should keep the existing GNU sysroot behavior. If no sysroot is configured, no sysroot option should appear.

constraints.grounded: Only the compiler-specific sysroot flag selection should change. `AutotoolsToolchain` and `GnuToolchain` must continue to honor `tools.build:sysroot`, preserve forward-slash normalization of the configured path, keep emitting the existing GNU `--sysroot` form for non-`qcc` compilers, and keep omitting `sysroot_flag` when the sysroot configuration is absent or falsy.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be narrowly scoped to how sysroot flags are formatted for the chosen compiler. Existing sysroot behavior for non-QNX or non-`qcc` builds must not regress, and builds without a sysroot configuration must continue behaving as before.

behavior: `AutotoolsToolchain` now inspects the configured compiler when deriving `sysroot_flag` from `tools.build:sysroot`.
`GnuToolchain` now inspects the configured compiler when deriving `sysroot_flag` from `tools.build:sysroot`.
If `settings.compiler` is `qcc` and `tools.build:sysroot` is set, the emitted `sysroot_flag` uses the qcc-compatible `-Wc,-isysroot,<normalized-path>` form.
If `settings.compiler` is not `qcc` and `tools.build:sysroot` is set, the emitted `sysroot_flag` remains `--sysroot <normalized-path>`.
If `tools.build:sysroot` is not set or evaluates as empty, both toolchains leave `sysroot_flag` unset.
acceptance_criteria: When a build uses `AutotoolsToolchain`, `tools.build:sysroot` is configured, and `settings.compiler` is `qcc`, the generated sysroot option should be emitted in qcc-compatible `-Wc,-isysroot,<path>` form.
When a build uses `GnuToolchain`, `tools.build:sysroot` is configured, and `settings.compiler` is `qcc`, the generated sysroot option should be emitted in qcc-compatible `-Wc,-isysroot,<path>` form.
When either toolchain is used with a configured sysroot and a compiler other than `qcc`, the generated sysroot option should continue to use the existing GNU `--sysroot <path>` form.
When a sysroot path contains backslashes, the emitted sysroot option should use the normalized forward-slash path.
When `tools.build:sysroot` is not configured or is empty, neither toolchain should emit a sysroot option.

task_15.title: Support recipe-based configuration package installs and batch config files
task_15.description: Conan 2.24.0 expands `conan config install-pkg` so users can install one or more configuration packages from `conanconfig.yml`, while storing installed configuration state as recipe references instead of package references. The update also makes configuration install order explicit: identical requests are skipped unless forced, safe additions and updates proceed normally, and reorder-causing updates are blocked unless the user explicitly forces them.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan config install-pkg` can manage configuration packages as an ordered set of recipe references, including installs declared in `conanconfig.yml`, and that it protects users from unsafe reordering of previously installed configuration layers unless they explicitly force the change.

expectation.grounded: `conan config install-pkg` should accept either a single configuration package reference or a `conanconfig.yml` path/directory containing a `packages` list and optional `urls` list. It should resolve each requested configuration as a `RecipeReference`, fetch and install the corresponding configuration packages, persist the installed configuration set as ordered recipe references, and write those same recipe references into lockfile `config_requires`. Reinstalling an identical ordered set should be skipped unless `--force` is supplied. Requests that add or update configuration packages without changing the order of already installed entries should succeed, while requests that would reorder existing installed configurations should raise `ConanException` unless `--force` is provided.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to install configuration from either one package reference or a config file that lists multiple packages, and Conan should remember that configuration by recipe identity rather than binary package identity. Safe updates should apply normally, duplicate requests should be ignored unless forced, and disruptive reordering of existing configuration layers should require an explicit override.

constraints.grounded: Configuration tracking and lockfile integration must use recipe references only, not package references or package IDs. Existing validation that configuration packages are of configuration package type and have no dependencies must remain in effect. The command must not silently change the relative order of already installed configuration packages; such changes are only allowed with `--force`. URL-based remote resolution must continue to work for direct installs and installs declared through `conanconfig.yml`.
constraints.conceptual: Do not make installed configuration state depend on a specific binary package instance, do not allow invalid configuration packages, and do not silently reshuffle previously applied configuration layers. Existing remote-based and lockfile-based configuration install workflows should keep working.

behavior: `conan config install-pkg` can now install multiple configuration packages from a `conanconfig.yml` file or directory, using the file's declared package list and optional remote URLs.
Installed configuration state is recorded as an ordered list of `RecipeReference` values rather than `PkgReference` values, so configuration identity no longer includes binary package IDs.
Lockfile `config_requires` entries are populated from the installed recipe reference list, including multi-package configuration installs.
If the requested configuration set is identical to the already installed ordered set, the command skips reinstallation unless `--force` is provided.
Adding a new configuration package or updating an existing one is allowed when the request preserves the order of previously installed configuration packages.
If a requested install would change the order of already installed configuration packages, the command fails with `ConanException` unless the user supplies `--force`.
Configuration packages used with this flow must still resolve to packages of configuration type and must not have dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan config install-pkg` with a single configuration package reference, it should install that configuration and remember it as a recipe reference.

When a user runs `conan config install-pkg` with a directory or `conanconfig.yml` that declares multiple packages, it should install those configuration packages in the declared order and make them the active configuration set.
When the requested configuration set exactly matches the currently installed ordered set, it should skip reinstallation unless `--force` is provided.

When a request adds a new configuration package or updates existing configuration packages without reordering previously installed entries, it should succeed and update the remembered configuration set and lockfile `config_requires` using recipe references.
When a request would reorder already installed configuration packages, it should fail unless the user explicitly provides `--force`.
When configuration-aware lockfile or package ID behavior reads installed configuration state, it should use recipe reference identity only and not depend on binary package IDs.

task_17.title: Fix option scoping for version-range install requirements
task_17.description: The upgrade corrects how unscoped CLI options are applied during `conan install` when the install target is expressed with a version-range requirement such as `dep/[*]`. Options should resolve to the intended package instead of being missed because the range pattern is treated as a literal version, and Conan should avoid emitting incorrect warnings in this scenario.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan install` correctly scopes a user-provided unscoped option to the single requested dependency when that dependency is declared with a version-range pattern such as `name/[*]`, and ensure that matching logic for version-pattern-based scoping recognizes version ranges instead of treating them as plain version strings.

expectation.grounded: When `conan install` is invoked with exactly one `--requires` dependency and an unscoped `-o/--options` assignment, Conan should scope the option to that dependency even if the requirement version is expressed as a version range like `[*]`. Matching between scoped option patterns and resolved requirements should treat bracketed versions as version ranges, using range containment or range intersection as appropriate, so the option applies to concrete versions and to requirements already represented by a version range. Conan should not emit false-positive warnings caused solely by misinterpreting the version-range pattern.
expectation.conceptual: If a user installs a single dependency using a version-range requirement and passes an option without an explicit package prefix, the option should still apply to that dependency exactly as it would for a fixed version. Version-range expressions should be interpreted semantically as ranges during option matching, and users should not receive misleading warnings when the dependency actually matches.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve existing behavior for fixed-version requirements, for requirements whose versions are already concrete, and for cases where option scoping relies on normal package-name matching. It should only alter version matching semantics for bracketed range patterns and should not require users to change the `conan install` CLI syntax for standard scoped or unscoped options.
constraints.conceptual: Existing installs that already work with explicit versions or explicit option scoping should continue to behave the same. The change should only broaden correct matching for range-based dependency expressions and should not introduce new ambiguity in how options are targeted.

behavior: An unscoped CLI option provided to `conan install` is automatically associated with the single requested dependency even when that dependency uses a bracketed version-range expression.
A bracketed version token in an option-scoping pattern is interpreted as a version range rather than as a literal version string.
If both the option pattern and the dependency requirement use version ranges, matching succeeds when the two ranges intersect.
If the option pattern uses a version range and the dependency resolves to a concrete version, matching succeeds when the concrete version falls within the requested range.
If the dependency requirement uses a version range and the option pattern uses a concrete version, matching continues to succeed only when the requirement range contains that version.
Warnings that were previously triggered because a version-range pattern failed literal version matching are suppressed when the dependency actually matches semantically.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan install` with exactly one `--requires=name/[*]` argument and passes `-o option=value` without a package prefix, the install should apply that option to `name` and complete without a mismatch caused by the `[*]` version pattern.
When option scoping targets a dependency using a bracketed version range and the resolved dependency version falls inside that range, the option should be considered applicable.
When both the option target and the dependency requirement are expressed as version ranges that overlap, the option should be considered applicable.
When the version constraints do not overlap or a concrete version is outside the targeted range, the option should not be applied.
When the only previous mismatch was caused by treating a version-range expression as a literal version, Conan should no longer emit a warning for that case.

task_16.title: Support multi-package config installs with safe ordering
task_16.description: Conan 2.24.0 expands configuration package installation so users can install multiple configuration packages from a conanconfig.yml source, while tracking installed configuration packages by recipe reference and blocking accidental reordering of existing configuration layers unless the user explicitly forces it.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan config install-pkg` can install configuration packages as an ordered set from `conanconfig.yml`, preserve the installed configuration stack by recipe reference, and reject order-changing updates unless the user explicitly forces the change.

expectation.grounded: `conan config install-pkg` should accept configuration package requirements loaded from `conanconfig.yml`, including the case where a directory is provided and the file is resolved from that directory. Any remote URLs declared by that configuration source should be added to the remotes used for the fetch. The installed configuration set should be compared and persisted as ordered RecipeReferences rather than PackageReferences. Re-running the command with an identical requested configuration set should skip re-installation unless `--force` is supplied. Adding a new configuration package or updating one without changing the relative order of already installed configuration packages should install normally. If the requested operation would reorder previously installed configuration packages, the command should raise a `ConanException` unless `--force` is provided.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare multiple configuration packages in a config file and install them together. Conan should treat the installed configuration stack as ordered, avoid reinstalling an unchanged stack unless forced, and protect users from accidental precedence changes by requiring explicit confirmation before a reorder is applied.

constraints.grounded: Do not silently reorder an existing installed configuration stack during `conan config install-pkg`. Preserve a single installed entry per configuration package name based on recipe-level identity, and keep the command compatible with the existing lockfile, remote-selection, and profile-based package resolution inputs used to fetch configuration packages.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must remain idempotent for unchanged configuration requests, additive for safe new entries, and explicit when a change would alter configuration precedence. It should continue to honor the user's normal package resolution context.

behavior: A configuration install can load multiple configuration package requirements from `conanconfig.yml` instead of being limited to a single directly provided package reference.
When a configuration source includes remote URLs, those remotes are included for the same installation operation.
Installed configuration packages are tracked and compared as an ordered set of recipe references rather than package references.
If the requested configuration set is identical to the already installed set, Conan skips re-installation unless `--force` is used.

If a requested addition or update does not change the effective order of already installed configuration packages, Conan installs the new or updated configuration packages and updates the stored ordered set.
If a requested install would change the order of previously installed configuration packages, Conan fails by default and only applies the reorder when `--force` is explicitly requested.
acceptance_criteria: When a user provides a `conanconfig.yml` that declares multiple configuration packages, Conan should resolve and install those configuration packages as one ordered configuration stack.

When that configuration source also declares remote URLs, Conan should be able to use those remotes for that install operation without requiring a separate prior remote setup step for the command to resolve the packages.
When the requested configuration stack matches the already installed stack, the command should leave the current configuration in place and skip re-installation unless `--force` is passed.

When a user adds a new configuration package or updates an existing one and the operation does not reorder previously installed configuration packages, the command should apply the change and persist the updated ordered stack.
When a requested install would reorder previously installed configuration packages, the command should reject the operation by default and only proceed if the user explicitly passes `--force`.

task_19.title: Handle external editables during workspace build
task_19.description: Conan 2.24.0 fixes a crash in `conan workspace build` when the dependency graph includes editable packages that are registered globally but are not part of the current workspace. Workspace builds should now treat those packages as external dependencies and process them through the external build flow instead of assuming workspace-local editable metadata exists.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan workspace build` completes successfully when the workspace depends on editable packages that were added globally but are not included in the current workspace, and that those external editables are handled through the normal external build flow instead of causing a crash.

expectation.grounded: During `conan workspace build`, packages reported as `Editable`, `EditableBuild`, or `Build` must be checked against the workspace editable registry before workspace-specific metadata is used. If a referenced package is not present in that registry, the command must treat it as external and run the existing external install/build flow instead of reading workspace-only editable data such as path or output folder. If the package is present in the workspace registry, the existing workspace editable behavior must continue unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: `conan workspace build` should distinguish between editables that belong to the current workspace and editables that are only registered globally. Workspace members should keep their current workspace build behavior, while external editables should be processed as external dependencies so the command finishes normally.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve current behavior for workspace-owned editables and for packages that do not rely on editable handling. Packages outside the workspace must not require workspace-local metadata to be available. External packages that need building during the workspace build must still be processed through the established external command path.
constraints.conceptual: The update should remove the crash without changing how normal workspace packages are built. Dependencies that are outside the workspace should be handled safely and consistently, and the command should not rely on workspace-only state for them.

behavior: `conan workspace build` no longer fails when the dependency graph includes a globally registered editable that is not part of the current workspace.
An editable package that is absent from the current workspace is treated as an external dependency instead of being assumed to have workspace metadata.
Packages outside the workspace whose binary state is `Build`, `Editable`, or `EditableBuild` are processed through the external install/build command path.
Packages that are part of the workspace continue to use workspace-specific editable path and output-folder information during the build flow.
acceptance_criteria: Given a workspace package that depends on a globally registered editable not added to the workspace, when `conan workspace build` runs, then the command should complete without crashing and should process that dependency as an external package.

Given a workspace package whose dependency is both editable and part of the workspace, when `conan workspace build` runs, then the dependency should continue to use workspace-specific editable handling.

When `conan workspace build` encounters a package outside the workspace whose binary state requires external build processing, it should invoke the external install/build flow instead of attempting workspace-only editable lookup.

task_18.title: Fix optimized compatibility mode across multiple remotes
task_18.description: Conan 2.24.0 fixes a regression in optimized compatibility-mode remote lookups so compatible binaries can be resolved correctly when more than one remote is configured. The update keeps the existing distinction between a remote that simply lacks the package and a remote that is unavailable.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that enabling `core.graph:compatibility_mode=optimized` works correctly when multiple remotes are configured, so Conan can resolve compatible binaries across all remotes without failing after the first remote lookup.

expectation.grounded: When `core.graph:compatibility_mode=optimized` is enabled, Conan should query each configured remote for the requested reference, collect available package IDs found in those remotes, and use the combined remote results for compatibility resolution. A missing reference in a given remote should remain non-fatal, while a remote connectivity failure should still be surfaced as `ConanConnectionError`.
expectation.conceptual: Optimized compatibility resolution should behave correctly in multi-remote setups: Conan should scan all configured remotes for compatible binaries, combine the results it finds, ignore remotes that simply do not contain the package, and still fail on real remote availability problems.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the current behavior where remotes that do not contain the requested reference are skipped. Do not suppress connection failures from remotes; those failures should still be reported and abort the operation. Preserve the optimized compatibility-mode flow and its use of remote package ID discovery.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the change to making multi-remote optimized compatibility lookups reliable, without altering normal compatibility behavior or weakening existing remote error handling.

behavior: With `core.graph:compatibility_mode=optimized`, compatibility resolution should inspect every configured remote during remote package ID discovery.
Compatible package IDs returned from different remotes should be aggregated so compatibility decisions can use the full set of available remote binaries.
If a remote does not contain the requested reference, the lookup should continue with the remaining remotes instead of treating that absence as an error.
If a remote cannot be reached during the lookup, Conan should report the remote availability problem and raise `ConanConnectionError`.
acceptance_criteria: When multiple remotes are configured and compatible binaries are available in more than one remote, running a command that uses `core.graph:compatibility_mode=optimized` should complete without crashing and should resolve compatibility using the remote results.
When the requested reference is absent from one configured remote but present in another, optimized compatibility lookup should continue and use the remotes that contain matching binaries.
When optimized compatibility lookup queries multiple remotes, it should consider compatible package IDs discovered in each remote rather than only the first successful remote query.
When any configured remote is unavailable during optimized compatibility lookup, the command should fail with `ConanConnectionError` instead of silently ignoring the connectivity issue.

task_20.title: Fix CMakeConfigDeps handling of separator-sensitive flags
task_20.description: The 2.24.0 update fixes a Conan CMakeConfigDeps regression where compile and link flags embedded in CMake generator expressions could be mis-handled when the flag values contained separators or multi-token shell-style arguments. Generated imported targets now preserve list-based flag entries so downstream CMake consumers receive valid, correctly scoped options.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.24.0 preserves compile and link flags emitted by CMakeConfigDeps when package metadata contains generator-expression-sensitive values, including separator-sensitive and multi-token flag entries, so downstream CMake projects consume the intended options without malformed target properties.

expectation.grounded: When Conan CMakeConfigDeps generates imported targets from package metadata, `cpp_info.cxxflags`, `cpp_info.cflags`, `cpp_info.sharedlinkflags`, and `cpp_info.exelinkflags` must be propagated as distinct CMake list items inside generator expressions rather than flattened into a space-delimited string. The generated `INTERFACE_COMPILE_OPTIONS` and `INTERFACE_LINK_OPTIONS` entries must remain valid when individual flags contain separators or shell-style multi-part arguments, while preserving existing scoping for C, C++, shared or module libraries, and executables.
expectation.conceptual: CMake dependency files generated after the upgrade should carry compile and link options exactly as package authors declared them, even when an option includes characters or formatting that CMake generator expressions treat specially. Consumers should see the right options applied to the right language or target type, without configuration-time breakage or silently altered flag boundaries.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not change the public configuration surface of CMakeConfigDeps or reinterpret flag ownership. `cxxflags` remain C++-only compile options, `cflags` remain C-only compile options, `sharedlinkflags` remain limited to shared and module library link options, and `exelinkflags` remain limited to executable link options. Existing package metadata that already worked without separator-sensitive content must continue to produce valid imported targets.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be a compatibility-preserving bugfix: it should only correct how options are encoded and forwarded, not broaden where they apply or require users to redefine package flags that were already supported.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps now preserves compile and link flag collections as list-separated values when embedding them in generated generator expressions.

Compile options originating from `cpp_info.cxxflags` and `cpp_info.cflags` continue to be applied only for their respective compile languages, but values containing separators or multi-token content are no longer merged into an invalid or ambiguous option string.

Link options originating from `cpp_info.sharedlinkflags` and `cpp_info.exelinkflags` continue to be scoped by target type, and separator-sensitive entries are forwarded without breaking generator-expression parsing.
Generated imported target properties remain valid for downstream consumers even when package flags include shell-style arguments or other content that depends on correct CMake list handling.
acceptance_criteria: When a package consumed through CMakeConfigDeps declares multiple `cpp_info.cxxflags` or `cpp_info.cflags`, and one or more entries contain separator-sensitive or multi-token content, the generated imported target should expose those options as separate compile options and keep them restricted to the correct source language.

When a package declares `cpp_info.sharedlinkflags` with separator-sensitive or shell-style multi-token entries, a downstream shared or module library target consuming the package should receive the intended link options without malformed CMake generator-expression handling.

When a package declares `cpp_info.exelinkflags` with separator-sensitive or shell-style multi-token entries, a downstream executable target consuming the package should receive the intended link options without malformed CMake generator-expression handling.
When package flags do not use separator-sensitive content, upgrading from 2.23.0 to 2.24.0 should preserve the same language and target-type scoping semantics for generated compile and link options.

task_21.title: Distinguish empty and unset EnvVars in generated shell scripts
task_21.description: Conan 2.24.0 fixes EnvVars script generation so shell activation scripts no longer treat an explicitly empty environment variable the same as an unset one. Generated .sh and .ps1 outputs now preserve intentional empty assignments while still removing variables that are meant to be unset.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that EnvVars-generated `.sh` and `.ps1` activation scripts distinguish between environment variables that are explicitly defined as empty and variables that are defined as unset, so upgrades preserve the intended shell environment state.

expectation.grounded: When `EnvVars` generates `.sh` or `.ps1` activation content, an entry that has defined values but resolves to an empty string must still be emitted as an empty-value assignment, while an entry with no values must be emitted as an unset or removal operation.
