This distinction should follow the `EnvVars` definition state rather than whether the rendered value is truthy.
expectation.conceptual: Shell activation scripts should preserve the semantic difference between setting a variable to an empty value and removing the variable from the environment. Users should see empty variables remain present but blank, while unset variables should be absent.

constraints.grounded: Do not change existing behavior for non-empty `EnvVars` assignments. Apply the corrected empty-versus-unset handling consistently to both generated `.sh` and `.ps1` scripts, and do not collapse explicit empty assignments into unset operations or convert unset operations into empty assignments.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the change to fixing the empty-versus-unset distinction without altering normal environment-variable assignment behavior. Both supported shell script formats should behave consistently.

behavior: Generated POSIX shell activation scripts keep explicitly empty `EnvVars` entries as empty-value assignments instead of treating them as unset.
Generated PowerShell activation scripts keep explicitly empty `EnvVars` entries as empty-value assignments instead of treating them as removed variables.
Variables that are actually unset in `EnvVars` continue to be emitted as unset or removal operations in generated activation scripts.
The choice between assignment and unset is determined by whether the `EnvVars` entry contains defined values, not by whether its rendered string is non-empty.
acceptance_criteria: When an `EnvVars` entry is explicitly defined as empty and a `.sh` activation script is generated, activating that script should leave the variable defined with an empty value rather than removing it.

When an `EnvVars` entry is explicitly defined as empty and a `.ps1` activation script is generated, activating that script should leave the variable defined with an empty value rather than removing it.
When an `EnvVars` entry is defined as unset, generated `.sh` and `.ps1` activation scripts should remove the variable from the environment rather than define it with an empty value.
When an `EnvVars` entry has a non-empty value, generated activation script behavior should remain the same as before the upgrade.

task_22.title: Prevent Workspace crashes when using per-package configuration
task_22.description: Conan 2.24.0 fixes a Workspace failure path so workspace-driven installs can accept per-package configuration, including package-pattern-scoped settings, without crashing during consumer/profile initialization.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `Workspace` operations do not crash when users pass per-package configuration, including configuration scoped to selected packages by pattern.

expectation.grounded: When a `Workspace` initializes its root `ConanFile`, per-package configuration must be handled in consumer context so dependency-targeted package patterns are accepted during profile initialization instead of causing the workspace flow to crash.
expectation.conceptual: Workspace installs should support the same per-package configuration behavior users expect from consumer workflows, allowing package-scoped settings without aborting the operation.

constraints.grounded: The change should preserve normal `Workspace` consumer initialization, keep valid per-package configuration applicable to matching packages, and only remove the crash caused by processing that configuration in the wrong context.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should eliminate the crash without changing the meaning of valid per-package configuration or altering unaffected workspace behavior.

behavior: `Workspace` initializes its root consumer context as a consumer before applying profiles and configuration.
Per-package configuration, including package-pattern-scoped settings, can be passed through workspace flows without triggering the previous crash.
Dependency-scoped configuration remains eligible to apply to matching packages during workspace installation instead of failing during setup.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs a `Workspace` operation with per-package configuration, the operation should complete its initialization path without crashing solely because that configuration was provided.
When per-package configuration is scoped to matching dependency packages in a `Workspace`, the configuration should be accepted during workspace setup.
When no per-package configuration is supplied, existing `Workspace` behavior should remain unchanged.

task_23.title: Fix version-range matching in replace_requires
task_23.description: Conan 2.24.0 fixes replace_requires so rules whose match pattern uses a version range are evaluated correctly against dependencies declared with either fixed versions or version ranges. Compatible replacements should now be applied instead of being skipped, reducing missed substitutions and resulting dependency graph conflicts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that replace_requires correctly matches and replaces dependencies when the replacement pattern uses a version range, including dependencies declared with an exact version and dependencies declared with a version range, while leaving incompatible requirements unchanged.

expectation.grounded: When a replace_requires pattern specifies a version range, Conan should interpret that pattern as a range matcher rather than as a literal version. For requirements with an exact version, replacement should occur only if the version is contained in the pattern range. For requirements that already use a version range, replacement should occur only if the pattern range intersects the requirement range. Name and other reference-component matching should continue to apply as before, and successful matches should be reflected in normal dependency graph resolution behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to define replace_requires rules with version ranges and have those rules reliably affect all compatible dependencies, regardless of whether the dependency was declared as a single version or as a version range. Incompatible dependencies should remain untouched.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter existing behavior for exact-version or wildcard replace_requires patterns beyond this range-matching fix. A range-based pattern must not replace a requirement unless the exact version is contained in the pattern range or the two ranges overlap. Non-version matching parts of the reference should continue to gate whether a replacement applies.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to correct matching semantics for range-based replacement rules. It must preserve existing replacement behavior outside this case and avoid applying replacements to incompatible dependencies.

behavior: replace_requires should treat a pattern version expressed as a version range as a range-based matcher.
A range-based replace_requires pattern should replace a dependency declared with a fixed version only when that fixed version is inside the pattern range.
A range-based replace_requires pattern should replace a dependency declared with a version range only when the pattern range and the dependency range overlap.
If a range-based pattern is incompatible with the dependency's fixed version or version range, no replacement should be applied.
Existing matching behavior for non-range patterns and other reference components should remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given a replace_requires rule whose pattern uses a version range and a dependency declared with a compatible fixed version, when dependency resolution runs, then the configured replacement should be applied.
Given a replace_requires rule whose pattern uses a version range and a dependency declared with an incompatible fixed version, when dependency resolution runs, then no replacement should be applied.

Given a replace_requires rule whose pattern uses a version range and a dependency declared with a compatible version range, when dependency resolution runs, then the configured replacement should be applied.

Given a replace_requires rule whose pattern uses a version range and a dependency declared with a non-overlapping version range, when dependency resolution runs, then the dependency should remain unchanged.
When a compatible range-based replacement is applied, the resolved dependency graph should use the replacement target instead of the original requirement.
